short: Open-vocabulary acoustic sensing on glasses (M05) and a one-speaker paired corpus (M11) are standard; voiced-data gains follow 2020 EMG work; one-speaker, one-run tests lag the field (M12).
position: The paper [@zhang2026sonispeech] moves eyewear acoustic sensing (M05) from command sets to open-vocabulary sentences and releases a one-speaker paired voiced and silent corpus (M11). Both are standard: open vocabulary is new for acoustic sensing (closest earlier system: 54 sentences [@luo2020acoustic]), but one speaker and one run cannot support an ahead verdict, and the 9,000 silent utterances are 1.2 times SSR7000 [@kimura2022ssr7000]. Its two findings, poor voiced-to-silent transfer (M04) and lower silent WER when voiced data are added (M03), follow the direction silent EMG showed in 2020 [@gaddy2020digital]. The evaluation (M12) is behind: one speaker, held-out sessions and one run, where earlier acoustic-sensing work held users out [@zhu2007ultrasonic; @luo2020acoustic; @zhou2025m2silent]. The 26.3% silent WER is a floor for this corpus, not evidence beyond this speaker.
